title: Rationale for and Impact of Increased Rental Occupancy Cap for HDB Units
what_it_is: Rationale for and Impact of Increased Rental Occupancy Cap for HDB Units

sections.label: HDB occupancy cap questions
sections.summary: Questions ask whether neighbour disputes correlate with HDB occupancy numbers and whether the January 2024 cap increase will raise disputes.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether there is any correlation or increase in neighbour disputes with regard to the number of occupants living in a HDB unit over the past five years; (b) whether the Ministry foresees that the increased rental occupancy cap for HDB units from January 2024 will result in more of such disputes; and (c) if so, how will HDB intervene to manage it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development with regard to the increased rental occupancy cap for HDB units from January 2024 (a) whether the Ministry foresees a rise in neighbour disputes and community disamenity, given the rationale for a reduced occupancy cap in HDB flats from nine to six as previously announced in 2018; and (b) whether HDB is sufficiently equipped to resolve any rise in complaints from such disamenity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) whether the Ministry can provide details on why the number of unrelated occupiers in a residential unit is increased from six to eight; and (b) what mitigation measures are taken to address the concerns of neighbours as a result of this increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development in each of the last five years (a) what is the number of cases of infringements of the occupancy cap on the number of persons allowed in (i) HDB flats and (ii) private residential properties respectively; and (b) what is the number of cases of unauthorised renting out of HDB flats.

sections.label: Housing completions and rent stabilising
sections.summary: Close to 100,000 public and private units will be completed from 2023 to 2025, and rent increases moderated in the third quarter of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Close to 100,000 public and private residential units will be completed from 2023 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We have also more than doubled PPHS supply to about 2,000 since 2021 and will further double it to about 4,000 units by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Public and private housing rents have showed recent signs of stabilising, with the quarterly increase in public and private housing rents moderating to 1.9% and 0.8% respectively in the third quarter of 2023, from 3% and 2.8% respectively in the previous quarter.

sections.label: Eight unrelated persons allowed
sections.summary: From 22 January 2024, these accommodations may house up to eight unrelated persons, up from the current cap of six.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: From 22 January 2024, these accommodations will be allowed to house up to eight unrelated persons, up from the current cap of six unrelated persons.

sections.label: URA private property occupancy enforcement
sections.summary: Private property owners must register with URA to house more than six persons, and URA took action against an average of 244 cases yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Similarly, owners of private residential properties must first register with the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) to authorise their properties to accommodate more than six persons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: URA undertakes regular inspections to ensure compliance with the prevailing occupancy cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Over the past five years, URA has taken action against an average of 244 cases per year for breaches of the occupancy cap in private residential properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor the demand and supply of open market rentals as well as residents’ feedback on disamenities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: These will be taken these into consideration when reviewing whether the relaxed occupancy cap should be extended beyond 2026.

sections.label: HDB rental rules and inspections
sections.summary: HDB rental rules and non-citizen quotas apply, about 16% of rented flats reach the six-person cap, and HDB inspects almost 500 flats monthly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For example, in HDB estates, who can rent a flat and a bedroom; and there are also non-citizen quotas that we have put in place and these rules apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I also, earlier, mentioned that only about 16% of the rental flats that have been rented out are reaching the six unrelated persons occupancy cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: At the same time, we are also putting in place measures to minimise potential disamenities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I mentioned earlier that those landlords who want to take advantage of this temporary relaxation have to apply to both HDB, prior to renting out, as well as to URA to increase to that eight unrelated persons occupancy cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Just to share with the Member, HDB investigates all feedback received and conducts routine planned inspections of almost 500 flats per month.

sections.label: Rental neighbour dispute feedback share
sections.summary: Feedback on neighbourly disputes from rental is about 1.5% of total feedback received about nuisance from neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The number of feedback relating to neighbourly disputes as a result of rental, is about 1.5% of the total feedback received about nuisance from neighbours.

sections.label: HDB whole flat rentals
sections.summary: About 58,000 HDB whole flats are rented out, roughly 5% of about one million sold flats, and 16% of these go to six unrelated occupants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, if the Senior Minister of State can elaborate on that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I said that about 58,000 of HDB whole flats are rented out and this is only about 5% of the approximately one million sold flats islandwide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And of these 58,000 HDB whole flats that are rented out, only 16% are rented out to six unrelated occupants.

sections.label: Non-citizen quota in HDB
sections.summary: The non-citizen quota is 11% at block level and 8% at neighbourhood level, with under 2% of neighbourhoods and about 1% of blocks affected as of December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We agree with the Member that it is important to maintain the Singaporean characteristics of an HDB estate and that is the reason why we have the non-citizen quota at 11% at block level and 8% at the neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And to share with the Member, as of December 2023, less than 2% of HDB neighbourhoods and about 1% of HDB blocks are affected by the non-citizen quota.

sections.label: Occupancy cap and enforcement complaints
sections.summary: The occupancy cap applies to all room rentals and tenant composition, and tenancy nuisance complaints are about 1.5% of all neighbour nuisance feedback.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The first one is a relatively factual one, whether the occupancy cap applies to flat or room rentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: It applies to all room rentals, tenant composition and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But a more important point he was asking was related to what Ms Denise Phua and Miss Cheryl Chan were asking as well, whether there is enough manpower for enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: But again, let me just set in context that, as of now, the complaints received resulting from tenancy rental, feedback on nuisance between neighbours is about 1.5% of all the total number of feedback received from nuisances caused by neighbours.

sections.label: Non-citizen quota for whole flats
sections.summary: The non-citizen quota applies for whole flat rentals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For the non-citizen quota, it applies for whole flat rentals.
